claims.statement: `GithubIssueService` extends `TypertRemoteService` and is registered under the cordis service key `githubIssue`, exposing seven `@Remote` endpoints; the package ships no browser half (it declares `dsh.bundle` but not `dsh.client`, and `src/client.ts` is a pure type projection), so it is a host backend consumed by UI plugins rather than a feature a user can open.

`static inject` lists only `llm`: `telemetry`, `storageDomain`, `sessionController`, `agents`, and `agentDefaultModel` are read structurally via `ctx.get` / `optionalService`, so the plugin activates on its own bundle and each of those capabilities degrades to a stable failure or a documented limitation instead of blocking activation.

Both model-backed methods resolve a route before calling anything: an unresolvable route returns `route-missing` and no model call is attempted, while a failed stream becomes `llm-failure` whose message names the provider, model, and preserved DSH code; `optimizeIssue` validates a blank description (`empty-input`) before route resolution and `generateReport` has no input validation.

Each generated report's title comes from the model output's first `## ` heading, falling back to `Telemetry failures in <pluginIds>` for `generateReport` and `New issue` for `optimizeIssue`; labels are fixed (`['bug','telemetry']` and `['bug']` respectively) and the results are frozen.

`prefilledIssueUrl` enforces its length budget on the composed URL, not on the body: it composes `title`/`body`/`labels` with `URLSearchParams`, shortens the body by at least the measured overflow per pass until the URL fits (bounded by 32 passes), appends `prefillTruncationNote` so the body reads as partial, and falls back to a body that is only the note when the note alone exceeds the budget; a `maxPrefillUrlLength` of 0 or less disables shortening entirely.

The prefill URL validator is narrower than the transport's repository parser: it requires exactly `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` (returning `invalid-url` otherwise), while `GithubIssueClient` accepts any host and takes the API origin from `apiBaseUrl`, so an Enterprise deployment can file and list issues but cannot produce a prefill link.

`createIssue` completes all local validation before any HTTP request — a non-string or blank title returns `invalid-request`, labels are trimmed with empty entries dropped, and the body goes through `issueBody`, which strips the leading `## title` heading the optimizer repeats so the filed issue does not show its title twice.

`GithubIssueFailureCode` is the caller-facing contract for the intake paths and deliberately keeps `auth-missing` (no credential configured) separate from `auth-failure` (credential rejected); `prefilledIssueUrl`'s `invalid-url` sits outside that union as the prefill path's own code.

The `generateReport` user prompt is built only from the facts the analysis carries (plugins, analysis window, totals, and per-group anchor/count/error/route/last-failure-time/attempts), and every fact the analysis does not carry is written as `not recorded` rather than omitted; the paired system prompt forbids proposing mechanisms the analysis does not evidence and forbids asking for extra collection.

The GitHub credential is resolved once per process in the order explicit `token`, then `env[tokenEnv]` (skipped when the name is empty), then the standard output of `tokenCommand` (`gh auth token` by default, with a timeout and 64KB buffer); the resolution is cached, a command failure only warns and counts as no credential, and the token is never logged.

Intake state is one durable row — the local day the last pass completed plus the issues already dispatched — declared as storage domain `github_issue_intake` (version 0) with a single `state` table keyed `intake` and zod validation; the domain module is imported dynamically because `@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-domain` is an optional peer, and without storage the service falls back to a frozen empty row with `intakePersistent` false.

`[Service.init]` opens the state, returns when `autopilotEnabled` is false, warns and skips the check when no durable state exists, and otherwise runs `startupIntake` un-awaited so a slow or unreachable GitHub cannot hold up host boot; a failed pass only warns so the day is retried at the next startup.

A pass commits its local day only after listing succeeded — a failed list returns the client failure untouched so no day is recorded — and `commitIntakeState` updates the in-memory row first, then writes durably, warning that a later pass may re-dispatch when the write fails.

De-duplication is by issue number, independent of the day: numbers already in the state are reported in `skipped` and never dispatched again, dispatch history is capped at 500 records, and a per-issue dispatch failure is collected in `failures` while the pass itself still returns `ok: true`.

Dispatch creates the Session through `sessionController.create` (so the deployment's preset and workspace policy apply), queues the rendered prompt via the Agent handle's `followup` to wake the driver, and renames the Session best-effort; a missing controller or registry yields `session-unavailable`, while a failed create, a created Session without a published Agent, or a refused prompt yields `dispatch-failed`, and a rename failure only logs.

The dispatch prompt is the configured `autopilotPrompt` template with `{number}`, `{title}`, `{url}`, `{body}`, and `{labels}` substituted, and an unrecognized placeholder is left visible so a template typo cannot disappear silently.

"Today" is the configured IANA zone's calendar day (`localDayKey` via `Intl.DateTimeFormat`); the zone is re-read per use, and an invalid zone falls back to the host zone with one warning per changed value so a typo cannot break the startup check or a dispatch.

Telemetry events are recorded under plugin id `github-issue` with the feature anchor `github-issue:<action>`: successes carry the route (and, for `generateReport`, the analyzed `pluginIds`), failures carry the preserved code/message/status plus route, and an unresolvable route is recorded as `NO_MODEL_ROUTE` — the same code `dsh-memo` uses so one suite-wide report can group both packages; without a telemetry service the calls behave identically.

Only three of the seven Remote methods have a shipped caller: the `ui-memo` controller calls `optimizeIssue` (with a route only when the user chose a model), `prefilledIssueUrl`, and `createIssue`; `generateReport` is called in-process by `dsh-memo`'s `analyzeLogs`, which passes its own resolved route as a request override, and `listClaimableIssues`, `dispatchIssue`, and `runIntake` are wire-addressable but have no caller besides the startup hook.

Configuration is split by effect timing: the eight `.volatile()` fields (`repoUrl`, `claimLabel`, `maxIssuesPerRun`, and the five `autopilot*` fields) are read from their refs where used so a settings write applies to the next call, while the other ten (`maxPrefillUrlLength`, `prefillTruncationNote`, `provider`, `model`, `token`, `tokenEnv`, `tokenCommand`, `tokenCommandTimeoutMs`, `apiBaseUrl`, `requestTimeoutMs`) are copied into instance fields at construction and require a remount; `autopilotEnabled` is read only in `[Service.init]`, so flipping it applies from the next host start.

Two change guardrails hold here: every Remote method declares exactly one parameter named `request` because the wire binding is `{ args: { request } }`, yet no source scan covers this package (the signature spec reads `dsh-memo`'s own `src/index.ts`), and `invariant.ts` registers an empty installer injecting `githubIssue` because the service owns its model calls and URL construction with no second authority — so these contracts rest on tests, not runtime invariants.
